blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — calcium carbonate supplement administration
stem: A client has been instructed to take 1,000 mg/day of supplemental elemental calcium and plans to take the entire amount as calcium carbonate at one time. Which teaching is most appropriate?

options.A: Divide the supplemental calcium into doses of 500 mg or less and take calcium carbonate with food because fractional calcium absorption falls as the amount taken at one time increases.
options.B: Take the full 1,000 mg at one time on an empty stomach because calcium carbonate absorption improves as the single elemental-calcium dose becomes larger.
options.C: Take calcium carbonate at bedtime without food because meals reduce absorption of this form and divided doses provide no absorption advantage over one large dose.
options.D: Dose size and meal timing have little effect on calcium absorption, so there is no reason to divide the 1,000-mg calcium-carbonate supplement.

rationale: Current NIH Office of Dietary Supplements guidance states that calcium absorption from supplements is highest with doses of 500 mg or less and the percentage absorbed decreases as the amount taken at one time rises. Calcium carbonate is absorbed best with food, whereas calcium citrate is less dependent on gastric acid. Therefore A is correct.
educational_objective: Optimize calcium-carbonate absorption by dividing supplemental elemental calcium into doses of 500 mg or less and taking calcium carbonate with food.

source_claim_supported: Calcium supplement absorption is highest at ≤500 mg elemental calcium per dose, and calcium carbonate is best absorbed with food.
